decisions.reason: It extends the core airfield-lighting business, likely required meaningful engineering and customer-integration investment, and the firm publicly framed it as setting a new standard, which favors continued commitment.

The surveillance display fits the firm's established integrated airport-operations offer and, with no clear failure signal, management would be inclined to continue supporting it rather than reverse course.

The training program is closely tied to the firm's service model and installed systems, so even if uptake were modest it is cheap to maintain and easy to justify as part of the broader solution portfolio.

This niche training course has the weakest visible commitment and is easiest to cut, but it still complements the firm's airfield-ground-lighting activities and would likely be retained unless clearly underperforming.

Airport collaboration software sits near the center of the firm's stated direction toward integrated, real-time, collaborative operations, so management has strong strategic and public reasons to persist with it.

As a flagship surveillance product explicitly presented as a focus of the firm's direction, it carries the strongest sunk-cost, reputational and strategic commitment and is therefore very unlikely to be withdrawn soon.
